description: A long first-row gap means the entire interval between successive row leaders is already covered by the current product frontier P_n = R_n C_n. This card proposes importing covering-system style interval certificates to show that such full coverage forces a rigid witness pattern that may be uniformly bounded.
mathematical_formalization: Let R_n={r_1,...,r_n}, C_n={c_1,...,c_n}, P_n={r_i c_j : i,j\le n}. If g_n=r_{n+1}-r_n, then [r_n+1, r_n+g_n-1] \subseteq P_n. Seek L such that any interval I of length > L cannot admit witness sets W(x)={(r,c)\in R_n\times C_n: rc=x} for every x\in I without violating an uncovered-set density bound.
analogical_connections: covering-system certificates for impossible dense covers
hypergraph shadow witnesses for consecutive constraints
proof certificates for SAT instances with highly correlated clauses
implementation_hypothesis: At each record gap, extract one minimal divisor witness per covered integer, compress the interval into a set-cover instance, and test whether the witness family necessarily induces a forbidden overlap pattern. A successful certificate search would produce a finite catalog of local obstructions whose nonappearance bounds g_n.
experiment_seed: Compute record gaps up to at least n=10^4, extract minimal witness families for each interior integer in those intervals, and cluster the certificates by overlap graph. A stable finite motif library would be strong evidence for a bounded-gap proof path.

closest_prior_art.title: Solution of the minimum modulus problem for covering systems
On the Erdős covering problem: the density of the uncovered set

novelty_claim: The new step is to treat consecutive covered integers in T as an endogenous covering system whose moduli and residues come from divisor witnesses, rather than from an externally prescribed congruence family.
differentiation: This is not a reimplementation of covering-systems work because the certificate objects are generated by the mex frontier and must explain a dynamic multiplication table, not a fixed family of residue classes.
